description: The shape libraries shipped with draw.io, the style-string properties that control how every shape and connector looks and behaves, and the editor features built on top of them - the Format panel, waypoints and connection points, tags, layers, pages and containers.

tools.name: General, Basic, Misc and Advanced shape libraries
tools.description: The always-on core libraries. General holds the everyday rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, diamond, cylinder, cloud, note, card, callout, list and container shapes; Basic adds geometric primitives (stars, crosses, arrows, banners, partial rectangles); Misc collects icons, curly braces, arcs and annotations; Advanced adds specialised vertices such as the manual input, tape and card variants used in flowcharts.
tools.usage: Left shape panel. Enable others with the "More Shapes" button at the bottom of the panel (Ctrl+Shift+K in some builds), or with the `libs=general;basic;misc;arrows2` URL parameter.
tools.example:
Style strings produced by these shapes:
`rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;` (rectangle)
`ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;`
`shape=cylinder3;boundedLbl=1;backgroundOutline=1;size=15;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;`
`shape=note;size=20;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;`
tools.notes: `whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;` appears in almost every modern style - it enables word wrapping and HTML labels.

tools.name: Arrows shape library
tools.description: Standalone arrow shapes (as opposed to connectors): single and double block arrows, callout arrows, bent and curved arrows, and the directional arrows used in process and marketing diagrams. Useful when an arrow must be a resizable shape with its own fill rather than an edge between two cells.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Other > Arrows, or `libs=arrows2`.

tools.name: Flowchart shape library
tools.description: The ANSI/ISO flowchart vocabulary: process, decision, terminator, predefined process, document, multi-document, manual input, manual operation, preparation, data/parallelogram, internal storage, direct data, stored data, delay, display, merge, extract, collate, sort, on-page and off-page connectors.
tools.usage: Left panel > Flowchart section, or `libs=flowchart`.

tools.name: Entity Relation shape library
tools.description: Database modelling shapes: entity tables with rows (as containers), the classic Chen entity/relationship/attribute symbols, and the crow's-foot notation connectors for one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many cardinality. Combine with `entityRelationEdgeStyle` connectors for readable ER diagrams.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Software > Entity Relation, or `libs=er`. SQL DDL can be imported with Arrange > Insert > Advanced > SQL.

tools.name: UML shape library
tools.description: The full UML set: class diagrams (classes with attribute/method rows, interfaces, enumerations, packages), sequence diagrams (lifelines, activation bars, synchronous/asynchronous/return messages, found/lost messages, combined fragments), activity diagrams (actions, forks, joins, decision nodes), state machines, use case diagrams, component and deployment diagrams.
tools.usage: Left panel > UML section, or `libs=uml;uml25`.
tools.example:
Class with rows:
`swimlane;fontStyle=1;align=center;verticalAlign=top;childLayout=stackLayout;horizontal=1;startSize=26;horizontalStack=0;resizeParent=1;collapsible=1;marginBottom=0;html=1;`
Lifeline:
`shape=umlLifeline;perimeter=lifelinePerimeter;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;container=1;collapsible=0;`
Inheritance edge:
`endArrow=block;endSize=16;endFill=0;html=1;`

tools.name: BPMN shape library
tools.description: Business Process Model and Notation 2.0 shapes: start, intermediate and end events with their trigger markers (message, timer, error, signal, conditional), tasks with type and marker decorations, gateways (exclusive, parallel, inclusive, event-based, complex), pools and lanes, data objects and stores, and sequence/message/association flows.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Business > BPMN, or `libs=bpmn;bpmn2`.

tools.name: AWS shape libraries
tools.description: Amazon Web Services architecture icons in several generations - AWS 2017 (aws3), AWS 2019/2021 (aws4) and AWS 2025 - covering compute, storage, database, networking, security, analytics, machine learning and management services, plus the group frames (VPC, subnet, availability zone, region, account) used for reference architectures.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > AWS 19 / AWS 17 / AWS 25, or `libs=aws4;aws3`.

tools.name: Azure shape library
tools.description: Microsoft Azure service icons and the older Azure/Microsoft Integration stencil sets, covering compute, storage, networking, identity, databases, AI, IoT and DevOps services, plus generic Microsoft product icons for Office 365, Dynamics and Windows.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Azure, or `libs=azure;mscae`.

tools.name: Google Cloud Platform shape library
tools.description: GCP product icons (Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Run, Spanner and the rest) together with the official GCP card and group styles used in Google's own reference architecture diagrams.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Google Cloud Platform, or `libs=gcp2;gcp3`.

tools.name: Cisco, Network and Rack shape libraries
tools.description: Physical and logical network diagramming. Cisco and Cisco19 provide the vendor's router, switch, firewall and wireless icons; the Network library has generic devices, clouds, servers and media; and the Rack library provides 19-inch rack frames whose unit-height shapes snap into place for data-centre elevation drawings.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Cisco / Cisco 19 / Network / Rack, or `libs=cisco;cisco19;networking;rack`.
tools.example:
Rack frame (a container with a unit grid):
`shape=rack;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#666666;container=1;collapsible=0;childLayout=rack;allowGaps=1;marginLeft=9;marginRight=9;marginTop=21;marginBottom=22;textColor=#666666;numDisp=off;`

tools.name: Kubernetes shape library
tools.description: The official Kubernetes icon set: control-plane components (API server, scheduler, controller manager, etcd), workload resources (pod, deployment, replica set, stateful set, daemon set, job, cron job), services and networking (service, ingress, endpoint, network policy), storage (PV, PVC, storage class) and the cluster/namespace group frames.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Kubernetes, or `libs=kubernetes`.

tools.name: C4 shape library
tools.description: Simon Brown's C4 model notation: person, software system, container and component boxes (internal and external variants), plus relationship edges carrying a technology label. The shapes use HTML labels with a name, a technology line and a description line, driven by the `dFontSize` and `dText` style keys.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Software > C4, or `libs=c4`.
tools.example:
`rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;labelBackgroundColor=none;fillColor=#438DD5;fontColor=#ffffff;align=center;arcSize=10;strokeColor=#3C7FC0;metaEdit=1;resizable=1;html=1;` with a label such as: `API Application
[Container: Java and Spring MVC]

Provides the JSON API
`
tools.notes: C4 shapes are `metaEdit=1`, so double-clicking opens a structured property dialog rather than the plain label editor.

tools.name: ArchiMate shape library
tools.description: The ArchiMate 3 enterprise-architecture notation: business, application, technology, physical, motivation, strategy and implementation layer elements with their standard colours and corner icons, plus the ArchiMate relationship types (composition, aggregation, assignment, realization, serving, access, influence, triggering, flow, specialization, association).
tools.usage: More Shapes > Business > ArchiMate 3 / ArchiMate, or `libs=archimate3;archimate`.

tools.name: Mockups, Bootstrap, Android and iOS shape libraries
tools.description: UI wireframing sets. Mockups provides sketchy browser windows, forms, buttons, tabs, menus and device frames; Bootstrap supplies web component wireframes matching the Bootstrap grid; Android and iOS provide the platform's controls, bars and screen frames for app mockups.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Software > Mockups / Bootstrap / Android / iOS, or `libs=mockup;bootstrap;android;ios`.

tools.name: Floorplan, Electrical, Sitemap and other specialist libraries
tools.description: The long tail of bundled libraries: Floorplans (walls, doors, windows, furniture, sanitary fittings), Electrical (circuit symbols, logic gates, resistors, transistors, IEC/ANSI variants), Sitemap (web site structure), Gantt, Mind Map, Venn, Infographic, Signs, Flags, Clip Art, Atlassian, Office, Veeam, Salesforce, IBM, Alibaba Cloud, Oracle Cloud and more.
tools.usage: More Shapes dialog, grouped by category (Business, Networking, Software, Engineering, Other). Each has a `libs=` key such as `floorplan`, `electrical`, `sitemap`, `mockup`, `veeam2`, `salesforce`.

tools.name: Custom shape libraries (.xml) and the Shapes dialog
tools.description: Any set of styled shapes can be saved as a reusable library. File > New Library creates one, shapes are dragged into it, and it is stored as an XML file (`<mxlibrary>[{"xml":"...","w":120,"h":60,"title":"Server"}]</mxlibrary>`) that colleagues load with File > Open Library. The `clibs=` URL parameter and the `defaultCustomLibraries` configuration key preload them automatically.
tools.usage: File > New Library... / File > Open Library from > Device or URL. Edit the Shapes dialog with the More Shapes button; preload with `clibs=Uhttps%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fteam.xml`.
tools.example:
1. Style your standard service box exactly.
2. File > New Library, drag the shape in, name it "Service", Save as `team-shapes.xml`.
3. Share the file; colleagues use File > Open Library from > Device, or you host it and add `&clibs=Uhttps%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fteam-shapes.xml` to their editor URL.

tools.name: Style string syntax
tools.description: Every cell's appearance and behaviour is one semicolon-separated string of `key=value` pairs stored in the mxCell's `style` attribute. A leading bare word (with no `=`) names the base shape or a named style, and later keys override earlier ones. Because the string is plain text it can be generated, templated and diffed, which makes it the main lever for programmatic styling.
tools.usage: Edit > Edit Style (Ctrl+E) on a selected cell, or the `style` attribute of an `<mxCell>` in the XML.

parameters.name: Leading token
parameters.description: `ellipse`, `rhombus`, `triangle`, `swimlane`, `text`, `image`, or `shape=mxgraph.<library>.<name>` for a stencil.

parameters.name: html=1
parameters.description: Allows HTML markup in the label - required for line breaks, bold and tables in labels.

parameters.name: whiteSpace=wrap
parameters.description: Wraps the label inside the shape's width instead of letting it run on one line.

parameters.name: Order
parameters.description: Later keys win, so appending `;fillColor=#ff0000` to a style overrides any earlier fillColor.

tools.name: Fill style properties
tools.description: Control the interior of a shape: `fillColor` (hex, a colour name, or `none`), `gradientColor` and `gradientDirection` for two-colour gradients, `opacity` for the whole cell, `fillOpacity` for the fill alone, `fillStyle` for the hand-drawn hatch patterns, and `backgroundOutline` / `glass` for the decorative overlays some stencils support.
tools.usage: Edit Style keys, or the Format panel > Style tab (Fill colour swatch, Gradient checkbox, Opacity slider).

parameters.name: fillColor
parameters.description: `#dae8fc`, `none`, or `default`. `none` makes the shape transparent but still selectable.

parameters.name: gradientColor / gradientDirection
parameters.description: Second colour and direction (north, south, east, west).

parameters.name: opacity / fillOpacity
parameters.description: 0-100. `opacity` fades the whole cell including its stroke and label.

parameters.name: fillStyle
parameters.description: With sketch style: auto, solid, hachure, cross-hatch, dots, dashed, zigzag-line.

tools.name: Stroke style properties
tools.description: Control a shape's or edge's outline: `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `dashed` and `dashPattern` for dash sequences, `rounded` and `arcSize` for corner rounding, `shadow`, `perimeterSpacing` for a gap between the outline and attached edges, and `sketch`/`curveFitting` for the hand-drawn look.
tools.usage: Edit Style keys, or Format panel > Style tab (Line colour, width, dashed/dotted buttons, Rounded and Shadow checkboxes).

parameters.name: strokeColor / strokeWidth
parameters.description: Outline colour (or `none`) and thickness in pixels.

parameters.name: dashed / dashPattern
parameters.description: `dashed=1` plus e.g. `dashPattern=8 8` or `1 4` for dotted.

parameters.name: rounded / arcSize
parameters.description: `rounded=1` with `arcSize` as a percentage (or absolute for edges).

parameters.name: shadow
parameters.description: `shadow=1` adds the default drop shadow.

tools.name: Text and label style properties
tools.description: Control the label: `fontSize`, `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontStyle` (a bit mask: 1 bold, 2 italic, 4 underline), `align` and `verticalAlign` inside the shape, `labelPosition` and `verticalLabelPosition` to move the label outside the shape, `labelBackgroundColor` and `labelBorderColor`, `spacing`/`spacingTop`/`spacingLeft`, `textOpacity`, `textDirection` and `overflow`.
tools.usage: Edit Style keys, or Format panel > Text tab.

parameters.name: fontStyle
parameters.description: Bit mask: 0 none, 1 bold, 2 italic, 3 bold+italic, 4 underline, 8 strikethrough (combined additively).

parameters.name: labelPosition / verticalLabelPosition
parameters.description: Set to `center`/`bottom` with `align=center;verticalAlign=top` to place the caption under an icon.

parameters.name: verticalAlign
parameters.description: top, middle, bottom.

parameters.name: overflow
parameters.description: `hidden`, `fill`, `width`, `block` - how a long label behaves relative to the shape bounds.

tools.example:
Icon with a caption beneath it:
`shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon;resIcon=mxgraph.aws4.lambda;html=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#232F3E;fontStyle=1;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;align=center;verticalAlign=top;`

tools.name: Shape selection keys (shape=, image=, stencil=)
tools.description: Choose which graphic is drawn. `shape=` names a built-in shape or a stencil from a library (`mxgraph.<library>.<name>`); `image=` renders an image shape from a URL or data URI; `stencil=` embeds a compressed custom stencil directly in the style; `sketch=1` renders in the hand-drawn style; and `resIcon`/`prIcon`/`symbol`-style keys select a sub-icon within a family stencil.
tools.usage: Edit Style; or drag a shape from a library and press Ctrl+E to read the style it produced.

parameters.name: shape=mxgraph.<lib>.<name>
parameters.description: A stencil from a bundled library, e.g. `mxgraph.kubernetes.icon`.

parameters.name: image=
parameters.description: `shape=image;image=https://example.com/logo.png;` - also accepts `data:image/png;base64,...`.

parameters.name: stencil=
parameters.description: A base64/deflate-encoded stencil XML embedded in the style itself.

parameters.name: sketch=1 / curveFitting=1 / jiggle=2
parameters.description: Hand-drawn rendering of the same shape.

tools.name: Behaviour and geometry style keys
tools.description: Keys that change how a cell behaves rather than how it looks: `container=1` makes it accept children, `collapsible=0/1` and `startSize` control folding and title height, `resizable`, `movable`, `editable`, `deletable`, `rotatable`, `connectable` and `cloneable` gate user interaction, `points=[[x,y,perimeter]]` defines fixed connection points, `perimeter=` chooses the outline function used to attach edges, `direction=` rotates directional stencils, and `childLayout=` applies an automatic layout to children.
tools.usage: Edit Style keys; several also appear in Format panel > Arrange tab and the right-click > Edit menu.

parameters.name: container / collapsible / startSize
parameters.description: Turn a shape into a container with a title bar of the given height.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: `points=[[0.5,0,0],[1,0.5,0],[0.5,1,0],[0,0.5,0]]` - four fixed anchors at the edge midpoints.

parameters.name: perimeter
parameters.description: `ellipsePerimeter`, `rhombusPerimeter`, `trianglePerimeter`, `parallelogramPerimeter`, `hexagonPerimeter2`, `lifelinePerimeter`, `none`.

parameters.name: childLayout
parameters.description: `stackLayout`, `treeLayout`, `flowLayout`, `tableLayout`, `rack` - auto-arranges children.

parameters.name: movable / resizable / deletable / editable
parameters.description: 0 disables that interaction, which is how template furniture is protected.

tools.example:
A stacked container whose children auto-arrange:
`swimlane;html=1;childLayout=stackLayout;horizontal=1;startSize=26;horizontalStack=0;resizeParent=1;resizeParentMax=0;resizeLast=0;collapsible=1;marginBottom=0;`

tools.name: Edge routing styles (edgeStyle)
tools.description: Chooses the algorithm that routes a connector. `orthogonalEdgeStyle` produces right-angled routes that avoid shapes and is the usual default; `elbowEdgeStyle` (with `elbow=horizontal|vertical`) makes a single elbow; `entityRelationEdgeStyle` is the side-entry style used in ER diagrams; `isometricEdgeStyle` routes at 30 degrees for isometric drawings; `segmentEdgeStyle` keeps user segments; omitting edgeStyle gives a straight line, and `curved=1` smooths whatever route is chosen.
tools.usage: Edit Style on an edge, Format panel > Style tab > Waypoints dropdown, or set `defaultEdgeStyle` in the configuration JSON.

parameters.name: edgeStyle
parameters.description: orthogonalEdgeStyle, elbowEdgeStyle, entityRelationEdgeStyle, isometricEdgeStyle, segmentEdgeStyle, or omitted for straight.

parameters.name: curved / rounded
parameters.description: `curved=1` draws smooth curves; `rounded=1` rounds the orthogonal corners.

parameters.name: orthogonalLoop
parameters.description: Routes self-loops orthogonally.

parameters.name: elbow
parameters.description: `horizontal` or `vertical` for elbowEdgeStyle.

tools.name: Arrowhead style keys
tools.description: Control the ends of a connector. `endArrow` and `startArrow` choose the marker - `classic`, `classicThin`, `block`, `blockThin`, `open`, `openThin`, `oval`, `diamond`, `diamondThin`, `box`, `halfCircle`, `async`, `cross`, `ERone`, `ERmany`, `ERoneToMany`, `ERzeroToOne`, `ERzeroToMany`, `dash`, `baseDash` or `none`. `endFill`/`startFill` make them solid or hollow and `endSize`/`startSize` set their size.
tools.usage: Edit Style on an edge, or Format panel > Style tab > the two arrow dropdowns.

parameters.name: endArrow / startArrow
parameters.description: Marker name, or `none` for a plain line.

parameters.name: endFill / startFill
parameters.description: 1 filled, 0 hollow - `endArrow=block;endFill=0` is UML inheritance.

parameters.name: endSize / startSize
parameters.description: Marker size in pixels (default 6).

tools.name: Edge endpoint and routing keys (exitX/entryX, jettySize, jumpStyle)
tools.description: Pin and shape a connector's route. `exitX`/`exitY` and `entryX`/`entryY` (0-1 relative to the source/target bounds) fix which point the edge leaves and enters, with `exitDx`/`exitDy` for a pixel offset and `exitPerimeter=0` to ignore the shape outline. `jettySize` sets the length of the straight stub leaving a shape, `jumpStyle` (`arc`, `gap`, `sharp`, `line`) and `jumpSize` draw line hops where edges cross, and `noEdgeStyle=1` freezes a manually routed edge.
tools.usage: Drag an edge endpoint onto a green connection point to set exitX/entryX automatically, or set them in Edit Style. Format panel > Style tab has Line jumps.

parameters.name: exitX / exitY / entryX / entryY
parameters.description: 0..1 fractions of the shape's width/height, e.g. `exitX=1;exitY=0.5` leaves the right-hand middle.

parameters.name: exitPerimeter / entryPerimeter
parameters.description: 0 attaches exactly at the point rather than at the perimeter intersection.

parameters.name: jettySize
parameters.description: `auto` or a pixel value - the length of the initial perpendicular segment.

parameters.name: jumpStyle / jumpSize
parameters.description: How crossing edges are drawn: arc, gap, sharp or line.

tools.name: Edge labels and multiple labels
tools.description: An edge can carry a main label plus any number of additional labels, each stored as a child mxCell with `edgeLabel` style and a relative geometry along the edge (x from -1 to 1) with an offset. Use them for cardinalities, conditions, protocols and port numbers. `labelBackgroundColor` keeps the text readable where it crosses the line.
tools.usage: Double-click an edge to edit its main label; double-click at a point along the edge, or right-click > Add Label, to add an extra one. Drag a label to reposition it.

parameters.name: edgeLabel style
parameters.description: `edgeLabel;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;resizable=0;points=[];`

parameters.name: mxGeometry x / y / offset
parameters.description: x = -1 (source) to 1 (target) along the edge; offset moves it perpendicular.

parameters.name: labelBackgroundColor
parameters.description: A solid background behind the text, usually `#ffffff` or `none`.

tools.example:
<mxCell id="lbl" value="yes" style="edgeLabel;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;resizable=0;points=[];" vertex="1" connectable="0" parent="e1">
  <mxGeometry x="-0.4" relative="1" as="geometry">
    <mxPoint as="offset" />
  </mxGeometry>
</mxCell>

tools.name: Format panel - Style tab
tools.description: The right-hand inspector's first tab for the current selection: fill and line colours, opacity, gradient, rounded/shadow/sketch/glass/comic toggles, line width and dash pattern, waypoint routing, arrowheads and line jumps for edges, plus the palette of preset colour schemes and the Edit Style button. For a container it also exposes the collapsible and layout options.
tools.usage: View > Format Panel (Ctrl+Shift+P), then the Style tab with a cell selected.
tools.example:
1. Select several shapes.
2. Click a colour scheme swatch in the Style tab - fill and stroke are set together to a matched pair.
3. Click Edit Style to see exactly which keys changed.

tools.name: Format panel - Text tab
tools.description: Typography for the selection: font family, size, colour, bold/italic/underline, alignment and vertical alignment, label position relative to the shape, word wrap, text formatting (lists, super/subscript), spacing around the text, and the global text direction. Changes here write the fontFamily/fontSize/fontColor/fontStyle/align keys into the style string.
tools.usage: Format Panel > Text tab with a cell selected (or with a label being edited).
tools.example:
1. Select every node (Ctrl+Shift+I).
2. Text tab: font Inter, size 13, colour #1A1A1A, alignment centre/middle.
3. Right-click > Edit Style shows `fontFamily=Inter;fontSize=13;fontColor=#1A1A1A;`.

tools.name: Format panel - Arrange tab
tools.description: Geometry and structure for the selection: exact size and position, angle, flip, align and distribute buttons, z-order, group/ungroup, copy size, autosize, and the container/collapsible settings. When nothing is selected it becomes the Diagram tab with page size, grid, background and paper settings.
tools.usage: Format Panel > Arrange tab.
tools.example:
1. Select a shape.
2. Arrange tab: set Size 160 x 60 and Position 120, 80 - the same as right-click > Edit Geometry.
3. Click "Copy Size", select other shapes and click "Paste Size" to normalise them.

tools.name: Copy Style, Paste Style, Edit Style and Set as Default Style
tools.description: Reuse an exact appearance. Copy Style and Paste Style transfer the whole style string between cells; Edit Style (Ctrl+E) shows it for direct editing; Set as Default Style makes the current cell's style the default for newly created shapes or edges in this diagram; Clear Default Style resets it. The `defaultVertexStyle` and `defaultEdgeStyle` configuration keys do the same thing permanently.
tools.usage: Right-click a cell > Edit Style (Ctrl+E) / Copy Style (Ctrl+Alt+C) / Paste Style (Ctrl+Alt+V) / Set as Default Style (Ctrl+Shift+D).
tools.example:
1. Style one box exactly as required.
2. Right-click > Set as Default Style - every new shape you draw now matches.
3. For a permanent team default, put the same keys in `defaultVertexStyle` in Extras > Configuration.

tools.name: Sketch, Rough and Comic styles
tools.description: Hand-drawn rendering modes. The Sketch theme (`ui=sketch`) changes the whole editor chrome and turns on rough rendering by default; per-shape, `sketch=1` with `curveFitting=1;jiggle=2` gives the rough.js look, `fillStyle=` picks a hatch pattern, and the older `comic=1` gives the wobbly-outline comic style. Useful for wireframes and early-stage diagrams that should not look finished.
tools.usage: Format panel > Style tab > Sketch checkbox; whole-editor sketch mode with the `sketch=1` or `ui=sketch` URL parameter; `rough=1` forces rough rendering.

tools.name: Waypoints and connection points
tools.description: Two different things that shape a connector. A waypoint is a fixed bend point on the edge, added by dragging the middle of a segment and removed with right-click > Clear Waypoints. A connection point is a fixed anchor on a shape (the small green crosses, defined by the `points=` style key), which turns a floating connection into an `exitX/entryX` pair so the edge always leaves the same spot.
tools.usage: Drag an edge segment to create a waypoint; right-click > Clear Waypoints to remove them. Alt+Shift+P toggles the display of connection points; hold Alt while dragging an endpoint to ignore them.
tools.example:
1. Hover a shape's edge until green crosses appear.
2. Drag from the right-hand cross to the target's left-hand cross.
3. Ctrl+E on the edge shows `exitX=1;exitY=0.5;entryX=0;entryY=0.5;`.
tools.notes: Floating connections (no exitX/entryX) let draw.io pick the shortest route as shapes move; fixed points keep the diagram stable but may cross other shapes.

tools.name: Tags
tools.description: Free-text labels attached to cells that let a viewer show and hide subsets of a diagram without using layers. Tags are stored in the cell's `tags` attribute (via Edit Data), toggled from Extras > Edit Diagram or the Tags panel, and can be driven from the URL with `tags={"prod":1,"dev":0}` or from a link so a single diagram serves several audiences.
tools.usage: View > Tags (or Extras > Tags), the `tags=` URL parameter, and the `toggleTags`/`hideTags`/`showTags` link actions on a shape.
tools.example:
1. Select the production-only shapes, Edit > Edit Data, add property `tags` = `prod`.
2. Open View > Tags and untick `prod` to hide them.
3. Publish a viewer link with `&tags=%7B%22prod%22%3A0%7D` to share the simplified view.

tools.name: Layers
tools.description: Each page has one or more layers; every cell belongs to exactly one. Layers can be renamed, reordered, hidden, locked, duplicated and merged, and cells are moved between them with right-click > Edit > Move to Layer. In the viewer, layers appear as toggles when `layers=1` is set, which makes them the standard way to build a step-by-step or before/after diagram.
tools.usage: View > Layers (Ctrl+Shift+L). Right-click a cell > Edit > Move to Layer... Viewer toggle with the `layers=1` URL parameter or the Publish dialog.
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+Shift+L, add layers "base", "step 1", "step 2".
2. Put each stage's shapes on its own layer.
3. Publish with Lightbox + Layers so the reader can step through.
tools.notes: A layer is an mxCell whose parent is cell 0; every shape's `parent` is the layer's id (or a container inside it).

tools.name: Pages
tools.description: A single .drawio file holds any number of pages, each a separate `<diagram>` element with its own mxGraphModel, page setup and layers. Pages are added, renamed, duplicated, reordered and moved between files from the tab bar at the bottom, and shapes can link to another page so the viewer navigates between them.
tools.usage: The + button and page tabs at the bottom of the editor; right-click a tab for Rename, Duplicate, Delete, Move Page, Insert Page. Select a page in the viewer with `page=2` (index) or `page-id=<id>`.
tools.example:
1. Right-click the page tab > Rename to "Overview".
2. Add a second page "Detail".
3. On the overview, select a box, Ctrl+K and link it to the "Detail" page.
tools.notes: CLI export defaults to the first page; use `-a/--all-pages`, `-p/--page-index` or `-g/--page-range` to control which pages are rendered.

tools.name: Containers, swimlanes, pools and tables
tools.description: Shapes that hold other shapes. A container (`container=1`) accepts children that move with it; a swimlane adds a title bar (`startSize`) and is the basis of BPMN pools and lanes; a table uses `childLayout=tableLayout` with row and cell children so rows and columns resize together. Containers can be collapsed, their children auto-arranged with `childLayout=stackLayout`, and they can be laid out independently of the rest of the page.
tools.usage: Drag a shape onto a container to add it as a child (hold Alt to drop it on top instead). Right-click > Edit > Add Lane / Add Row / Delete Lane. Format panel > Arrange tab > Container checkbox turns any shape into one.

parameters.name: startSize
parameters.description: Height (or width for vertical) of the swimlane title bar.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: 1 for a horizontal title bar (vertical lanes), 0 for a vertical title bar (horizontal lanes).

parameters.name: childLayout
parameters.description: `stackLayout` auto-stacks children, `tableLayout` drives table rows and cells.

parameters.name: resizeParent / resizeLast / collapsible
parameters.description: How the container reacts when children change and whether it can be folded.

tools.example:
Horizontal pool with lanes:
`swimlane;html=1;horizontal=0;startSize=20;childLayout=stackLayout;resizeParent=1;resizeParentMax=0;horizontalStack=0;`
Then right-click > Edit > Add Lane Below for each participant.
